questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle respond to directional changes?

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond to your movements. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery when rain starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars. This gives you the best grip on the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Use your mirrors. You do not need to look over your shoulder unless you see something unusual.
Either use your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This makes sure no other vehicles are in your way.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Not talk or move unnecessarily.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers to avoid talking and unnecessary movement while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should motorcyclists generally travel?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In single-file formation.
Side-by-side.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when turning or entering a highway. Side-by-side riding is dangerous because both riders lose their escape routes.

questions.question: When is there less traction available for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is leaning.
When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as during a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do it carefully.

questions.question: If another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It links the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied.
It brakes automatically based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It links the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you apply the rear brake pedal, it automatically connects the front and rear brakes together. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white with red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Feels uncomfortable.
Provides protection in a crash.
Should not stand out to other motorists.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash, keep you comfortable, and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will merge together.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if the bike stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Allow you to blend in with traffic.
Provide an escape route.
Encourage others to use your lane.

questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind from other vehicles, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should keep others from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: To reduce crash risk, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Scan your path ahead.
Be ready to act to avoid a hazard.
Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: Always make sure others can see you to reduce crash risk. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Only the front brake should be used.
The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.
Only the rear brake should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Helps protect your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.explanation: The rear brake is usually operated with your right foot.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time than usual to stop and speed up.
The same amount of time to stop and speed up as it usually does.
More time than usual to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time than usual to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows a motorcycle down. With a passenger on board, your motorcycle takes longer to speed up and slow down than when you ride alone.

questions.question: A helmet will give you the most protection if it is all of the following, except:

options.text: U.S. DOT-compliant.
Loose-fitting.
Free of defects.

questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best if it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Mirrors show everything around you perfectly.
Mirrors do not show your blind spots.
You should not use mirrors except when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, restaurants, and hospitals.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight through your lane to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your angle could move you into another lane and cause a collision.

questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist ride in the lane?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic. This keeps you away from the passing driver and is safer for both of you.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in the lane?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view ahead and helps other drivers see your move.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When lights flash at a railroad crossing, stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard for drivers to see a motorcycle's turn signals, the rider should:

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk the horn to tell other drivers about turns.
Use hand signals.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is important to clearly show other drivers your intentions.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are not very strong.
Is always acceptable.
May affect your riding abilities and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding abilities and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how new medications may affect your riding.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid heavy traffic areas.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road well ahead of your motorcycle. This helps you spot and avoid hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.
